source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 1 May 1924, p. 7 ("A Derry withdrawal. No contests for County Council"); Londonderry Standard, 2 May 1924, p. 8 ("Derry County Council elections: no contest")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned unopposed: 'Mr. J. Steele Hanna has withdrawn his nomination for the Derry No. 1 Division ... Mr. J. R. Scott, D.L., the former member for this division, is now returned unopposed' (Belfast News-Letter, 1 May 1924, p. 7; Londonderry Standard, 2 May 1924, p. 8).

note: Triennial election of Londonderry County Council. Nominations were received on 24 April 1924 (Belfast News-Letter, 25 April 1924). Seventeen divisions were returned unopposed: J. Steele Hanna withdrew his nomination for Derry No. 1, so J. R. Scott, D.L., the sitting member, was returned unopposed and there was no contest anywhere in the county (Belfast News-Letter, 1 May 1924, p. 7; Londonderry Standard, 2 May 1924, p. 8). No nominations were received for Claudy or Faughanvale, which the council filled on 11 June by appointing C. A. Nicholson and George Leeke (Derry Journal, 13 June 1924, p. 6). No party labels were printed. Filed on 1924-05-30, the polling day for county council and rural district elections in Co. Londonderry that year (confirmed); previously filed under 1924-05-29 (verification 5 Nov 2026). The News-Letter of 25 April 1924 had listed Scott and Hanna as opposing candidates; Hanna withdrew before the poll. The first meeting of the new council (Derry Journal, 13 June 1924, p. 6) lists J. R. Scott, D.L., among the members. Returned unopposed.
